title: The Console calendar does not read `calendar.initialDate`, so it still opens on today
body:
domain:spec#4 · marchtian · session_017ihL2fi9zfJhUTubyJYb6V

Filing gate: ② the consumer half of #28021. The spec half declares the key; this card is the renderer that reads it. It lands after that PR merges.
Reach: any calendar view whose records fall months ahead. HotCRM's renewals calendar opens on an empty month (#27386 row 3). Once the spec key ships, an author who writes `calendar.initialDate: 'next_record'` or `'{next_month_start}'` gets a view that parses and saves, and still opens on today.
Reader who acts: `domain:ui`.
Seam: spec:`CalendarConfigSchema.initialDate` → renderer:`ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx#ObjectCalendar`

## Observed (this repo, `ui/` tree, on main at 549203d040)
- `ObjectCalendar` sets its current date with `useState(new Date())` (`ObjectCalendar.tsx`, the `currentDate` state). It reads no anchor from the calendar config.
- The spec PR for #28021 adds an optional `initialDate` to `CalendarConfigSchema`. It takes one of two forms: a record anchor, `'first_record'` or `'next_record'`, or a wrapped, known date-macro token such as `'{today}'`, `'{next_month_start}'` or `'{3_months_from_now}'` (the vocabulary is `DATE_MACRO_TOKENS` plus the parameterised grammar in `packages/spec/src/data/date-macros.zod.ts`). That schema is the list view's `calendar` block, and it is also the `object-calendar` node's `calendar` prop. `@object-ui/types` takes the block by reference, so the mirror accepts the key without an edit.

## Wanted
- `ObjectCalendar` reads `calendar.initialDate` where it seeds `currentDate`:
  - absent: today, as now.
  - a date-macro token: the period that holds the date the token resolves to when the calendar opens. Resolve it with the client resolver filter values already use (`resolveDateMacros()` in `@object-ui/core`), not a second one.
  - `'first_record'`: the period that holds the earliest `startDateField` value among the records the view selects, with its filter applied.
  - `'next_record'`: the period that holds the earliest `startDateField` value on or after the start of today.
  - When no record qualifies, today.
  - The period is the month, week or day of the active view mode.
- The renderer fetches only the visible range. So the two record anchors need their own one-row read: sort by `startDateField` ascending, limit 1, plus a lower bound for `next_record`. Seed once on mount. After that, user navigation owns the date.
- Copies that are owned by `ui/` and list the calendar block's keys, kept in step:
  - the `list-view` registry input description in `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx`, which feeds `sdui.manifest.json` and `content/docs/ui/components/plugins.mdx`;
  - the `object-calendar` registry `calendar` input description in `plugin-calendar`;
  - the hand-typed `calendar` options in `ui/packages/types/src/designer.ts`.
  Regenerate the manifest with `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`.
- Amend the `calendar` row note in `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`. It now says `initialDate` rides at planned strength. Change it to plain live, citing the read.

Dedupe words: calendar initialDate renderer, ObjectCalendar currentDate seed, calendar first_record next_record.

Related: #28021, #27386 (row 3).

Body refreshed 2026-10-30T15:31Z: the values follow the formula form the maintainer asked for on #28021 (a record anchor or a date-macro token; the bare `'today'` is gone). The triage comment 6523386496 carries no request for the body; its `Blocked-by:` line is kept.

Blocked-by: #28021
